title: MySQL Create Database
content:
-- Create a new database
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS school_db;               -- naya database banao

-- Select/use the database
USE school_db;                                         -- database select karo

-- Show all databases
SHOW DATABASES;                                        -- information dekho

-- Drop database (be careful!)
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS school_db;                     -- database delete karo

title: MySQL Create Table
content:
-- Create table with common data types
CREATE TABLE students (                                -- naya table banao
    id         INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,  -- unique auto id
    name       VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,           -- student name required
    age        INT CHECK (age > 0),             -- age must be positive
    class      VARCHAR(20),                     -- class e.g. 10th
    marks      DECIMAL(5,2) DEFAULT 0.00,       -- marks out of 100
    email      VARCHAR(150) UNIQUE,             -- unique email
    status     ENUM('active','inactive') DEFAULT 'active', -- agar value na di to yeh use hogi
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP     -- agar value na di to yeh use hogi
);

-- View table structure
DESCRIBE students;                                     -- table structure dekho

-- View create statement
SHOW CREATE TABLE students;                            -- naya table banao

title: MySQL Insert Data
content:
-- Insert single row
INSERT INTO students (name, age, class, marks, email)  -- data add karo
VALUES ('Alice', 20, '10th', 92.5, 'alice@example.com'); -- jo values insert karni hain

-- Insert multiple rows at once
INSERT INTO students (name, age, class, marks, email) VALUES -- data add karo
  ('Bob',     21, '11th', 78.0, 'bob@example.com'),
  ('Charlie', 19, '10th', 85.5, 'charlie@test.com'),
  ('Diana',   20, '12th', 95.0, 'diana@example.com'),
  ('Evan',    22, '11th', 74.5, 'evan@test.com');

-- Upsert: insert or update on duplicate
INSERT INTO students (email, name, marks)              -- data add karo
VALUES ('alice@example.com', 'Alice', 97)              -- jo values insert karni hain
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE marks = 97;                    -- data update karo

-- Check last inserted id
SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID();                               -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL Select Query
content:
-- Select all rows
SELECT * FROM students;                                -- data fetch karo

-- Select specific columns
SELECT name, marks FROM students;                      -- data fetch karo

-- Select with alias
SELECT name AS student_name, marks AS score FROM students; -- data fetch karo

-- Distinct values
SELECT DISTINCT class FROM students;                   -- data fetch karo

-- Count rows
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM students;                -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL Where Clause
content:
-- Basic WHERE condition
SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 80;               -- data fetch karo

-- WHERE with AND
SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 75 AND age >= 20; -- data fetch karo

-- WHERE with OR
SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks > 90 OR class = '10th'; -- data fetch karo

-- BETWEEN range
SELECT * FROM students WHERE marks BETWEEN 70 AND 90;  -- data fetch karo

-- LIKE pattern matching
SELECT * FROM students WHERE name LIKE 'A%';    -- starts with A
SELECT * FROM students WHERE name LIKE '%li%';  -- contains 'li'
SELECT * FROM students WHERE name LIKE '_ob';   -- 3 chars, ends ob

-- IN list
SELECT * FROM students WHERE class IN ('10th', '11th'); -- data fetch karo

-- NOT IN
SELECT * FROM students WHERE class NOT IN ('12th');    -- data fetch karo

-- IS NULL check
SELECT * FROM students WHERE email IS NULL;            -- data fetch karo
SELECT * FROM students WHERE email IS NOT NULL;        -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL Order By and Limit
content:
-- Sort ascending (default)
SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC;             -- data fetch karo

-- Sort descending (highest first)
SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;            -- data fetch karo

-- Sort by multiple columns
SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY class ASC, marks DESC; -- data fetch karo

-- Limit: top 5 students
SELECT * FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC LIMIT 5;    -- data fetch karo

-- Pagination: page 2 (5 per page)
SELECT * FROM students LIMIT 5 OFFSET 5;               -- data fetch karo

-- Shorthand pagination
SELECT * FROM students LIMIT 10, 5;  -- skip 10, take 5

title: MySQL Group By Having
content:
-- Count students per class
SELECT class, COUNT(*) AS total_students               -- data fetch karo
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY class;                                        -- group banao

-- Multiple aggregate functions
SELECT class,                                          -- data fetch karo
    COUNT(*)          AS total,                        -- rows count karo
    ROUND(AVG(marks), 2) AS avg_marks,                 -- average nikalo
    MAX(marks)        AS highest,                      -- maximum value
    MIN(marks)        AS lowest,                       -- minimum value
    SUM(marks)        AS total_marks                   -- total nikalo
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY class;                                        -- group banao

-- HAVING: filter after grouping (avg marks > 75)
SELECT class, AVG(marks) AS avg                        -- data fetch karo
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY class                                         -- group banao
HAVING AVG(marks) > 75                                 -- group filter karo
ORDER BY avg DESC;                                     -- sort karo

-- NOTE: WHERE filters BEFORE grouping, HAVING filters AFTER

title: MySQL Update
content:
-- Update single field
UPDATE students SET marks = 95 WHERE name = 'Alice';   -- condition lagao

-- Update multiple fields at once
UPDATE students SET marks = 98, class = '12th' WHERE id = 1; -- condition lagao

-- Increment value
UPDATE students SET marks = marks + 5 WHERE marks < 50; -- condition lagao

-- Update all rows in a class
UPDATE students SET status = 'inactive' WHERE class = '12th'; -- condition lagao

-- Conditional update using CASE
UPDATE students                                        -- data update karo
SET grade = CASE                                       -- naya value set karo
    WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'A'
    WHEN marks >= 75 THEN 'B'
    WHEN marks >= 60 THEN 'C'
    ELSE 'F'
END;

-- SAFE: always use WHERE in UPDATE to avoid updating all rows!

title: MySQL Delete
content:
-- Delete a specific row
DELETE FROM students WHERE id = 1;                     -- kis table se

-- Delete rows matching condition
DELETE FROM students WHERE marks < 33;                 -- kis table se

-- Delete multiple with IN
DELETE FROM students WHERE class IN ('11th', '12th');  -- kis table se

-- Delete all rows (table structure stays)
DELETE FROM students;                                  -- kis table se

-- TRUNCATE: faster delete, resets AUTO_INCREMENT
TRUNCATE TABLE students;

-- Drop entire table
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS students;                         -- table delete karo

-- WARNING: Always run SELECT first to preview what will be deleted!

title: MySQL Joins
content:
-- INNER JOIN: only matching rows from both tables
SELECT s.name, s.marks, c.course_name                  -- data fetch karo
FROM students s                                        -- kis table se
INNER JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id        -- tables jodo
INNER JOIN courses c    ON e.course_id = c.id;         -- tables jodo

-- LEFT JOIN: all students, even those not enrolled
SELECT s.name, c.course_name                           -- data fetch karo
FROM students s                                        -- kis table se
LEFT JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id         -- tables jodo
LEFT JOIN courses c    ON e.course_id = c.id;          -- tables jodo
-- unenrolled students will show NULL for course_name

-- RIGHT JOIN: all courses, even with no students
SELECT s.name, c.course_name                           -- data fetch karo
FROM students s                                        -- kis table se
RIGHT JOIN courses c ON s.class = c.class;             -- tables jodo

-- Self JOIN: employees with their manager
SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager           -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;          -- tables jodo

-- TIP: INNER = intersection, LEFT = all left + matching right (NULL if no match)

title: MySQL Indexes
content:
-- Create simple index (speeds up WHERE on marks)
CREATE INDEX idx_marks ON students(marks);             -- search fast karne ke liye

-- Unique index (no duplicate emails)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_email ON students(email);      -- duplicate values allowed nahi

-- Composite index (for queries filtering class AND marks)
CREATE INDEX idx_class_marks ON students(class, marks); -- search fast karne ke liye

-- Full-text index for text search
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX ft_name ON students(name);       -- search fast karne ke liye

-- Full-text search query
SELECT * FROM students                                 -- data fetch karo
WHERE MATCH(name) AGAINST('Alice' IN BOOLEAN MODE);    -- condition lagao

-- View all indexes on a table
SHOW INDEX FROM students;                              -- kis table se

-- Check if query uses index (look for 'ref' or 'index' in type column)
EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM students WHERE email = 'alice@example.com'; -- data fetch karo

-- Drop index
DROP INDEX idx_marks ON students;                      -- search fast karne ke liye

title: MySQL Alter Table
content:
-- Add new column
ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(15);     -- table modify karo

-- Add column at specific position
ALTER TABLE students ADD COLUMN dob DATE AFTER age;    -- table modify karo

-- Modify column type or size
ALTER TABLE students MODIFY COLUMN marks FLOAT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0; -- table modify karo

-- Rename column
ALTER TABLE students RENAME COLUMN phone TO mobile;    -- table modify karo

-- Drop column
ALTER TABLE students DROP COLUMN mobile;               -- table modify karo

-- Add index via ALTER
ALTER TABLE students ADD INDEX idx_class (class);      -- table modify karo

-- Add foreign key
ALTER TABLE students                                   -- table modify karo
ADD CONSTRAINT fk_dept
FOREIGN KEY (dept_id) REFERENCES departments(id)       -- doosre table se link karo
ON DELETE SET NULL ON UPDATE CASCADE;                  -- data update karo

title: MySQL Foreign Key
content:
-- Step 1: Create parent table
CREATE TABLE departments (                             -- naya table banao
    id   INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,               -- unique identifier — duplicate nahi ho sakta
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL                         -- empty nahi ho sakta
);

-- Step 2: Create child table with foreign key
CREATE TABLE employees (                               -- naya table banao
    id      INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,            -- unique identifier — duplicate nahi ho sakta
    name    VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,                     -- empty nahi ho sakta
    dept_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (dept_id) REFERENCES departments(id)   -- doosre table se link karo
        ON DELETE SET NULL   -- set NULL if dept deleted
        ON UPDATE CASCADE    -- update if dept id changes
);

-- Insert parent first, then child
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1, 'Engineering'), (2, 'Marketing'); -- data add karo
INSERT INTO employees (name, dept_id) VALUES ('Alice', 1), ('Bob', 2); -- data add karo

-- Join to see relationship
SELECT e.name, d.name AS dept                          -- data fetch karo
FROM employees e                                       -- kis table se
JOIN departments d ON e.dept_id = d.id;                -- tables jodo

title: MySQL Stored Procedure
content:
-- Stored Procedure: saved SQL code that can be called by name
-- Useful for reusable queries, business logic, and batch operations

DELIMITER //    -- change delimiter so semicolons inside don't end the statement

-- Create procedure with input parameter
CREATE PROCEDURE GetTopStudents(IN min_marks DECIMAL(5,2))   -- IN = input parameter
BEGIN                                                  -- transaction shuru karo
    -- Select students with marks above the given threshold
    SELECT name, class, marks                          -- data fetch karo
    FROM students                                      -- kis table se
    WHERE marks >= min_marks      -- use the input parameter in query
    ORDER BY marks DESC;          -- show highest marks first
END //

DELIMITER ;     -- restore normal delimiter

-- Call the procedure
CALL GetTopStudents(85);          -- get students with marks >= 85
CALL GetTopStudents(60);          -- get all passing students

-- Procedure with OUT parameter (returns a value)
DELIMITER //                                           -- statement end character badlo
CREATE PROCEDURE CountStudents(OUT total INT)   -- OUT = output parameter
BEGIN                                                  -- transaction shuru karo
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO total    -- INTO stores result into the parameter
    FROM students;                                     -- kis table se
END //
DELIMITER ;                                            -- statement end character badlo

CALL CountStudents(@total);       -- @total is a user-defined variable
SELECT @total AS total_students;  -- view the returned value

title: MySQL Transaction
content:
-- Start a transaction
START TRANSACTION;

  -- Transfer money: debit account 1
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE id = 1; -- condition lagao
  
  -- Credit account 2
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 500 WHERE id = 2; -- condition lagao

COMMIT;  -- Save both changes permanently

-- Transaction with ROLLBACK on error
START TRANSACTION;
  UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 500 WHERE id = 1; -- condition lagao
ROLLBACK;  -- Undo changes (error occurred)

-- SAVEPOINT: partial rollback
START TRANSACTION;
  INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1, 'Order A');            -- data add karo
  SAVEPOINT sp1;
  INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (1, 'Item X');  -- might fail
  ROLLBACK TO sp1;  -- undo only after savepoint
COMMIT;                                                -- changes save karo

title: MySQL Date Functions
content:
-- Current date and time
SELECT NOW();          -- 2024-01-15 10:30:00
SELECT CURDATE();      -- 2024-01-15
SELECT CURTIME();      -- 10:30:00

-- Extract parts
SELECT YEAR(created_at), MONTH(created_at), DAY(created_at) -- data fetch karo
FROM students;                                         -- kis table se

-- Format date
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(created_at, '%d/%m/%Y') AS formatted -- data fetch karo
FROM students;                                         -- kis table se

-- Date difference
SELECT DATEDIFF(NOW(), created_at) AS days_since       -- data fetch karo
FROM students;                                         -- kis table se

-- Add/subtract days
SELECT DATE_ADD(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AS next_month; -- data fetch karo
SELECT DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) AS last_year;  -- data fetch karo

-- Filter by year
SELECT * FROM students WHERE YEAR(created_at) = 2024;  -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL String Functions
content:
-- Case conversion
SELECT UPPER(name) AS upper_name FROM students;        -- data fetch karo
SELECT LOWER(name) AS lower_name FROM students;        -- data fetch karo

-- Concatenate strings
SELECT CONCAT(name, ' - Class: ', class) AS label FROM students; -- data fetch karo
SELECT CONCAT_WS(', ', name, class, email) AS csv FROM students; -- data fetch karo

-- Length
SELECT name, LENGTH(name) AS name_length FROM students; -- data fetch karo

-- Substring: extract part of string
SELECT SUBSTRING(name, 1, 3) AS short_name FROM students; -- data fetch karo

-- Trim whitespace
SELECT TRIM('  Alice  ');  -- 'Alice'

-- Replace
SELECT REPLACE(email, '@example.com', '@school.edu') FROM students; -- data fetch karo

-- Find position
SELECT INSTR(name, 'li') AS pos FROM students;         -- data fetch karo

-- NULL handling
SELECT IFNULL(email, 'no-email') FROM students;        -- data fetch karo
SELECT COALESCE(email, phone, 'no-contact') FROM students; -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL Subquery
content:
-- Students with marks above average
SELECT name, marks FROM students                       -- data fetch karo
WHERE marks > (SELECT AVG(marks) FROM students);       -- data fetch karo

-- Subquery with IN
SELECT name FROM students                              -- data fetch karo
WHERE id IN (                                          -- condition lagao
    SELECT student_id FROM enrollments WHERE course_id = 3 -- data fetch karo
);

-- EXISTS: check if related data exists
SELECT name FROM students s                            -- data fetch karo
WHERE EXISTS (                                         -- condition lagao
    SELECT 1 FROM enrollments e WHERE e.student_id = s.id -- data fetch karo
);

-- Subquery in FROM (derived table)
SELECT class, avg_marks FROM (                         -- data fetch karo
    SELECT class, ROUND(AVG(marks), 2) AS avg_marks    -- data fetch karo
    FROM students GROUP BY class                       -- kis table se
) AS class_avg                                         -- alias naam do
WHERE avg_marks > 80;                                  -- condition lagao

title: MySQL Views
content:
-- Create a view (saved query as virtual table)
CREATE VIEW top_students AS                            -- virtual table banao
SELECT name, class, marks                              -- data fetch karo
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
WHERE marks >= 85                                      -- condition lagao
ORDER BY marks DESC;                                   -- sort karo

-- Use view like a regular table
SELECT * FROM top_students;                            -- data fetch karo
SELECT * FROM top_students WHERE class = '10th';       -- data fetch karo

-- Create view with JOIN
CREATE VIEW student_courses AS                         -- virtual table banao
SELECT s.name, s.class, c.course_name                  -- data fetch karo
FROM students s                                        -- kis table se
JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id              -- tables jodo
JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id;                  -- tables jodo

-- Drop view
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS top_students;

-- NOTE: Views don't store data, they store the query

title: MySQL Information Schema
content:
-- Show all tables in current database
SHOW TABLES;                                           -- information dekho

-- Show table structure
DESCRIBE students;                                     -- table structure dekho

-- Detailed column info from information_schema
SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE, IS_NULLABLE, COLUMN_DEFAULT -- data fetch karo
FROM information_schema.COLUMNS                        -- kis table se
WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'students'                          -- condition lagao
  AND TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE();

-- Table sizes
SELECT TABLE_NAME,                                     -- data fetch karo
    TABLE_ROWS AS estimated_rows,                      -- alias naam do
    ROUND((DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) / 1024, 2) AS size_kb -- decimal round karo
FROM information_schema.TABLES                         -- kis table se
WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()                        -- condition lagao
ORDER BY size_kb DESC;                                 -- sort karo

-- Current user and database
SELECT USER(), DATABASE();                             -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL Create Table Teachers
content:

title: MySQL Create Table Employees
content:
-- Create employees table in MySQL
CREATE TABLE employees (                               -- naya table banao

    name        VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,                   -- full name (required)

title: MySQL Create Table Products
content:

content:
-- AND condition

SELECT * FROM students WHERE name LIKE 'A%';    -- starts with A

SELECT * FROM students WHERE email IS NOT NULL;        -- data fetch karo

title: MySQL Aggregate Functions
content:
-- All aggregate functions
SELECT
    COUNT(*)            AS total_students,             -- rows count karo
    COUNT(email)        AS with_email,                 -- rows count karo
    SUM(marks)          AS total_marks,                -- total nikalo
    ROUND(AVG(marks),2) AS avg_marks,                  -- average nikalo
    MAX(marks)          AS highest,                    -- maximum value
    MIN(marks)          AS lowest,                     -- minimum value
    STDDEV(marks)       AS std_deviation               -- alias naam do
FROM students;                                         -- kis table se

-- GROUP BY with aggregates
SELECT
    class,
    COUNT(*)            AS students,                   -- rows count karo
    ROUND(AVG(marks),2) AS avg,                        -- average nikalo
    MAX(marks)          AS highest,                    -- maximum value
    MIN(marks)          AS lowest                      -- minimum value
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY class                                         -- group banao
ORDER BY avg DESC;                                     -- sort karo

-- HAVING: only classes with avg > 80
SELECT class, AVG(marks) avg                           -- data fetch karo
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY class                                         -- group banao
HAVING avg > 80;                                       -- group filter karo

title: MySQL Self Join
content:
-- SELF JOIN: joining a table with itself
-- Use case: employee-manager relationships, category hierarchies

-- Create table where employees have manager_id (also an employee)
CREATE TABLE employees_mgr (                           -- naya table banao
    id         INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,         -- unique identifier — duplicate nahi ho sakta
    name       VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,                  -- empty nahi ho sakta
    role       VARCHAR(50),
    manager_id INT,                                  -- references same table's id
    FOREIGN KEY (manager_id) REFERENCES employees_mgr(id)  -- self-reference
);

-- Insert organizational hierarchy
INSERT INTO employees_mgr (name, role, manager_id) VALUES -- data add karo
    ('Director', 'CEO',       NULL),   -- top level: no manager
    ('Alice',    'Manager',   1),      -- reports to Director (id=1)
    ('Bob',      'Manager',   1),      -- reports to Director
    ('Charlie',  'Developer', 2),      -- reports to Alice (id=2)
    ('Diana',    'Designer',  2),      -- reports to Alice
    ('Eve',      'Tester',    3);      -- reports to Bob (id=3)

-- Self join: show each employee with their manager
SELECT
    e.name  AS employee,           -- alias 'e' for the employee side
    e.role  AS emp_role,                               -- alias naam do
    m.name  AS manager,            -- alias 'm' for the manager side (same table!)
    m.role  AS mgr_role                                -- alias naam do
FROM employees_mgr e               -- 'e' = employee instance
LEFT JOIN employees_mgr m          -- 'm' = manager instance (same table)
    ON e.manager_id = m.id         -- connect employee's manager_id to manager's id
ORDER BY e.manager_id;             -- group by manager

title: MySQL Duplicate Records
content:
-- Finding and removing duplicate records

-- Find duplicate email addresses
SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS occurrences   -- count how many times each email appears
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY email                           -- group by the potentially duplicated field
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1                      -- keep only groups with more than 1 row
ORDER BY occurrences DESC;              -- show most duplicated first

-- Find duplicate names
SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS count                         -- data fetch karo
FROM students                                          -- kis table se
GROUP BY name                                          -- group banao
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;                                   -- group filter karo

-- View all duplicate rows (including all columns)
SELECT * FROM students                                 -- data fetch karo
WHERE email IN (                                       -- condition lagao
    SELECT email FROM students    -- subquery finds duplicate emails
    GROUP BY email                                     -- group banao
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1           -- only emails appearing more than once
);

-- Delete duplicates keeping the row with the LOWEST id
DELETE s1
FROM students s1                                       -- kis table se
INNER JOIN students s2                                 -- tables jodo
    ON s1.email = s2.email        -- find rows with same email
    AND s1.id > s2.id;            -- keep the one with smaller id, delete the rest

-- Count unique vs total after cleanup
SELECT
    COUNT(*)              AS total_rows,      -- all rows
    COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS unique_emails,   -- unique email values
    COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS duplicates  -- how many were duplicates
FROM students;                                         -- kis table se
